D018-D011_h001.question:
I'm not exactly sure why I'm here. My husband, Mark, thinks I've been a bit off since ... a few months ago. It's hard to put a finger on it. I’ve been having these terrible dreams, some nights, it feels like I’m right back there, the fear is so real. I used to love our weekend hikes, but now, I just can't seem to get excited about anything.

Honestly, it feels like everyone around me just moved on. It’s like they don’t understand how much *that day* really changed things. If only certain people had been more careful, none of this would have happened. And the shock... sometimes it feels like it just happened yesterday. Then there are other days when I just can't make a decision – even picking out an outfit for a shoot feels impossible. And if someone touches me unexpectedly, even Mark, I just jump out of my skin. It’s all just so overwhelming.
D018-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h001.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h002.question:
It's been… I don’t know, maybe six months since I started feeling like this. It’s hard to pinpoint when exactly. I’m just not myself. Everything feels dull, like I’m watching my life from a distance. The things I used to enjoy, like playing with the kids or even just a quiet evening with my wife, they just don’t spark anything in me anymore. I keep replaying that day at the factory in my head, over and over, and I can't shake the feeling that I should have done something differently. I carry this… this shame, like a weight.

Then there are moments, out of nowhere, where I'm right back there. My heart pounds, and I can almost smell the smoke again. A sudden noise, or someone moving quickly in my periphery, and I jump out of my skin – it’s like I’m constantly on edge. My memory's gone to pot too; I forget where I put my keys or what I was just about to do. It’s like my brain just can’t focus on anything. My wife says I’m just stressed, and maybe she’s right. I just feel… off.
D018-D011_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h002.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h003.question: It’s been… a while now, I suppose, that things have felt off kilter. Months, certainly. My mind just feels foggy, like I’m constantly wading through mud, making it hard to focus on shelving or even recommending a good book. I just can't seem to get myself to start things anymore, even tasks I enjoy used to. It's frustrating because I know I should.
